caption:
Reach is not a result. Impressions are not a result. Engagement is not a result.

A customer is a result.

Every one of those first three can go up while your revenue stays exactly where it was. That's why they're on the report: they always have a good number available.

Here's the test I'd apply to any marketing report you receive. Can you draw a line from the number on the page to money in the bank? If you can't, it's a vanity metric wearing a suit.

The numbers that pass: cost per lead, cost per customer, close rate, revenue per channel.

Everything else is context at best, decoration at worst.

Free 20-minute audit in bio. You leave with the four that matter.
